opening.argument: The presentation gives step-by-step instructions to connect MetaMask and send ETH to a deployed contract, while linking that contract’s arbitrage activity to making money. It presents the process as repeatable—“You can do this all day long”—and claims that retrying with specified parameters “should work 100%” with a smaller profit. The wallet interface visibly shows a 0.1 ETH send, and the activity record displays a corresponding -0.1 ETH entry. These features promote the funded contract as a repeatable money-making method, although the available records do not establish who controlled the recipient, how the contract behaved, whether funds could be recovered, or that any profit was completed.
